title: Texas Indian Restaurant Chain Desi Chowrastha Opens Largest Location in Overland Park
excerpt: The 7,564-square-foot eatery at Corbin Park brings over 100 menu items — from dosas and biryanis to chaats and chai — to Johnson County's growing South Asian community.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Desi Chowrastha opens its first Kansas City-area location in Overland Park, Kansas.
  • The restaurant spans 7,564 square feet, making it the largest Indian eatery in Overland Park.
  • It offers over 100 menu items, including dosas, biryanis, and chaats.
  • Desi Chowrastha has 25 franchisees across multiple states in the U.S.
  • Prices range from $7.99 for tiffins to $52.99 for family packs.

A Texas Chain Plants Its Flag in Johnson County

The Kansas City area's Indian dining scene has a significant new entrant. Desi Chowrastha, a fast-growing Indian restaurant chain headquartered in Texas, has opened its first location in the metro at Corbin Park Retail Village in Overland Park. At 7,564 square feet, the restaurant is the largest Indian eatery in Overland Park, occupying the space left by Copps Pizza Company, which closed earlier this year.

The name itself tells a story. "Desi" refers to the people and cultures of India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh. "Chowrastha" means the intersection of four streets — a reference to the gathering places where communities congregate in South Asian towns. The restaurant aims to be exactly that kind of crossroads, combining a sit-down eatery with a market selling Indian groceries and snacks.

"A Menu That Runs Deep The "massive menu" descriptor is not an exaggeration."

A Menu That Runs Deep

The "massive menu" descriptor is not an exaggeration. Desi Chowrastha's offerings span more than 100 items across multiple categories. The tiffin section alone lists over 20 options, from sambar idli and thatte idli to upma, pongal, and poori bhaji, priced from $7.99 to $14.99. The dosa menu is even more extensive, with more than 25 varieties including masala dosa ($12.97), Mysore masala dosa ($14.15), guntur karam dosa, benne dosa, and even chocolate and Nutella dosas for the adventurous.

Biryanis form another pillar of the menu, with individual portions ranging from $13.99 to $18.99 and family packs that run from $39.99 to $52.99. The restaurant also serves chaats, curries, kabobs, and appetizers like vegetable pakora and samosas. Lassis and chai round out the beverage options.

Franchise Model Fuels National Expansion

Desi Chowrastha's arrival in Johnson County is part of a broader national expansion. The chain has 25 franchisees across the country, with locations in Texas, Virginia, Nevada, Georgia, Indiana, Arizona, and Illinois, and more under contract. It is a franchise model that reflects the growing demand for Indian food across the American heartland — not just in the coastal cities and university towns that were the first wave of Indian restaurant growth, but in suburban communities with expanding South Asian populations.

Menu Highlights
›Over 20 tiffin options available.
›More than 25 varieties of dosas offered.
›Biryanis priced from $13.99 to $18.99.
›Includes chaats, curries, kabobs, and appetizers.

Overland Park, the second-largest city in Kansas, has seen its Indian and South Asian population grow steadily, drawn by corporate employers and a suburban quality of life. The area around 135th Street and Metcalf Avenue has become something of an Indian dining corridor, with several restaurants and grocery stores serving the community. Desi Chowrastha's entry, with its scale and chain-backed resources, raises the competitive bar.

Open Late, Priced for Families

The restaurant operates on generous hours: 10 a.m. to 11 p.m. Monday through Thursday, 10 a.m. to midnight on Fridays, 9 a.m. to midnight on Saturdays, and 9 a.m. to 10:45 p.m. on Sundays. The pricing sits in the moderate range for Indian dining, with most individual dishes between $10 and $16. The family pack biryanis, which serve four to six people, offer value for larger gatherings — a practical consideration for the multi-generational Indian families that are a key customer base.

For Johnson County's Indian community, Desi Chowrastha's opening means one less reason to drive to the Indian grocery stores and restaurants clustered along Devon Avenue in Chicago or Hillcroft in Houston. For everyone else in Overland Park, it is an invitation to explore a cuisine that stretches far beyond butter chicken and naan.
